headline: No enforced disappearances or extrajudicial killings in last 6 months: Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed claims no political persecution has occurred since the current government took office, while discussing a new law to prevent disappearances.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated on Saturday that no one in Bangladesh has been subjected to enforced disappearance, extrajudicial killing, or political persecution over the last six months.

The remarks were made during a panel discussion organized by Mayer Daak at the National Museum auditorium in Shahbagh, held on the eve of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances.

Addressing the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh, the minister said an independent investigation found no evidence of political motive, suggesting instead that he may have been caught in conflicts between robber groups in the Sundarbans.
The minister also discussed the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act 2026, a new law designed to ensure victims can approach courts for justice and redress.
This upcoming law includes definitions of disappearance, investigation procedures, and the death penalty as the maximum punishment for perpetrators.
It also provides for compensation and ensures that heirs of disappeared persons receive property rights to support their families.
However, human rights activist Nur Khan Liton challenged these claims, alleging that eyewitness accounts and digital data indicate law enforcement involvement in Miraj Sheikh's case.
Liton demanded a transparent probe into the roles of the police and the Coast Guard, emphasizing that independent investigation is paramount for the new law to be effective.

Addressing the disappearance of Miraj Sheikh, the minister said an independent investigation found no evidence of political motive, suggesting instead that he may have been caught in conflicts between robber groups in the Sundarbans.

The minister also discussed the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act 2026, a new law designed to ensure victims can approach courts for justice and redress.

This upcoming law includes definitions of disappearance, investigation procedures, and the death penalty as the maximum punishment for perpetrators.

It also provides for compensation and ensures that heirs of disappeared persons receive property rights to support their families.

headline_marked: Rain likely to [[continue for five days]] across Bangladesh
headline: Rain likely to continue for five days across Bangladesh
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department predicts light to moderate rain and thunderstorms across most divisions, with cautionary signals issued for maritime ports.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has predicted that rainfall is likely to continue across the country for five days, as the monsoon remains fairly active.
Light to moderate rain or thunder showers, accompanied by temporary gusty winds, are expected in many places across the Rangpur, Mymensingh, Chattogram, and Sylhet divisions.
Rainfall is also expected in a few places across the Rajshahi, Dhaka, Khulna, and Barishal divisions, with moderately heavy falls occurring in some areas nationwide.
A low-pressure area has formed over the Northwest Bay and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coasts and is likely to move west-northwestwards.
Due to this weather system, the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra have been advised to hoist local cautionary signal-3.
caption:
